To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hepatocellular state of hydration modulates the PEPCK gene transcription, and that this modulation is independent of the cAMP and protein kinase C signaling systems, and independent of Na+ and Cl-.
anisotonic changes of the osmolarity of perfusion media and of the medium of cultured hepatoma cells affect PEPCK mRNA and protein levels.
the anisotonia effects on the PEPCK gene are independent of protein kinase C and of the intracellular cAMP concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the hepatic gluconeogenic enzyme phosphoenolpy-ruvate car boxykinase (PE-PCK).
the regulation of the gene expression of key enzymes of carbohydrate metabolism.
the regulation of gene expression and the role of cellular hydration as a regulatory parameter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aniso-osmotic exposure of hepatocytes affects PEPCK mRNA expression in a time- and concentration-dependent manner.
the anisotony effects on PEP CK mRNA levels are mediated by an unknown mechanism, independent of cAMP, protein kinase C or Na+ and Cl-.
the cellular hydration status is a determinant for the metabolic activity of the hepatocyte and that this is at least in part mediated at the level of gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatocellular water content is an important regulator of the expression of genes involved in the regulation of the hepatic carbohydrate metabolism.
the hepatocellular osmolarity affects the hepatic carbohydrate metabolism by modulating P-EPCK mRNA levels.
cellular hydration affects hepatic metabolism over a long term by modulating mRNA levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydration of hepatocytes affects the expression of the key gluconeogenic enzyme, PEPCK, by modulating PCK1 mRNA levels.
the cellular hydration state affects the hepatic mRNA levels of the key gluconeogenic enzyme PEPCK, and this is independent of protein kinase C or cAMP levels.
the cellular hydration state is an important determinant of the hepatic metabolism of carbohydrates.
